html:
SMTO-K8S-0005 — The Kubernetes certificate in your settings is empty or too large

GUID: d21ec56f-726d-4c01-9d8d-f40cb60f85d9
Slug: kubernetes-config-limit
Domain: K8S · Subsystem: k8s

What happened

  • SMTO reads the cluster's certificate from your Kubernetes settings to confirm the cluster is genuine. That certificate is empty, in the wrong form, or larger than SMTO accepts, so SMTO couldn't record the cluster. Your command wasn't blocked.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the person who manages Kubernetes access to check that the cluster certificate in the Gateway computer's Kubernetes settings file is filled in and complete. An empty or damaged certificate can't be used to confirm the cluster.
  2. If the certificate bundle is very large, have them keep only the certificates needed to trust this cluster. SMTO accepts at most 128 KB and 32 certificates for one cluster.
  3. Then ask the agent to run a read-only command such as kubectl get pods. A successful read-only command lets SMTO record the cluster with its corrected certificate.

What success looks like

  • The read-only command succeeds and SMTO keeps using that cluster in later steps.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages Kubernetes access. Don't remove the certificate or turn off certificate checking to make this go away.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The kubeconfig cluster's certificate-authority-data is not a string, exceeds the 256 KiB encoded limit, decodes to nothing, or exceeds the 128 KiB decoded CA limit.

What this means

  • Inline CA data is not a string, exceeds its encoded bound, decodes empty, or exceeds the raw CA byte limit. These are local configuration/observation checks, not proof of cluster reachability or command rollback. Optional observation failure cannot change the underlying command outcome; diagnostics perform no cluster operations.

Why this can happen

  • Inline CA data is not a string, exceeds its encoded bound, decodes empty, or exceeds the raw CA byte limit.

How to diagnose it

  • Check encoded and decoded size separately and retain only the required public trust chain.

How to fix it

  • In the Gateway node's kubeconfig, set certificate-authority-data to the base64 of a non-empty PEM bundle of at most 128 KiB holding only the cluster's CA certificates (1–32), or point certificate-authority at a CA file instead. Keep the chain needed to verify the server; do not remove verification.
  • Supply a valid nonempty public CA bundle within encoded and decoded size bounds.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A nonempty bounded public CA bundle passes discovery while preserving the required trust chain.

What not to do

  • Do not erase authoritative receipts or protected current input to conceal a size/capacity problem.

Technical notes

  • These are local configuration/observation checks, not proof of cluster reachability or command rollback. Optional observation failure cannot change the underlying command outcome; diagnostics perform no cluster operations.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
